passages.text: You are sons of the LORD your God; do not cut yourselves or shave your foreheads on behalf of the dead, for you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD has chosen you to be a people for His prized possession out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.
passages.sermon:
You are sons of the LORD your God.
Do not cut yourselves for the dead.
Do not shave your foreheads for the dead.
You are a people holy to the LORD your God.
The LORD your God has chosen you.
He chose you to be His special people.
He chose you out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.
passages.original: בָּנִ֣ים אַתֶּ֔ם לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֑ם לֹ֣א תִתְגֹּֽדְד֗וּ וְלֹֽא־ תָשִׂ֧ימוּ קָרְחָ֛ה בֵּ֥ין עֵינֵיכֶ֖ם לָמֵֽת׃ כִּ֣י עַ֤ם קָדוֹשׁ֙ אַתָּ֔ה לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ וּבְךָ֞ בָּחַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה לִֽהְי֥וֹת לוֹ֙ לְעַ֣ם סְגֻלָּ֔ה מִכֹּל֙ הָֽעַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃ס

passages.text: You must not eat any detestable thing.
passages.sermon:
God commands His people.
God says, "Do not eat anything detestable."
Do not eat food that is unclean or forbidden.
Obey this command from God.

passages.text: These are the animals that you may eat: The ox, the sheep, the goat, the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope, and the mountain sheep.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel special laws.
God chose Israel as His holy people.
God told Israel which animals they may eat.
You may eat the ox.
You may eat the sheep.
You may eat the goat.
You may eat the deer.
You may eat the gazelle.
You may eat the roe deer.
You may eat the wild goat.
You may eat the ibex.
You may eat the antelope.
You may eat the mountain sheep.
passages.original: זֹ֥את הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאכֵ֑לוּ שׁ֕וֹר שֵׂ֥ה כְשָׂבִ֖ים וְשֵׂ֥ה עִזִּֽים׃ אַיָּ֥ל וּצְבִ֖י וְיַחְמ֑וּר וְאַקּ֥וֹ וְדִישֹׁ֖ן וּתְא֥וֹ וָזָֽמֶר׃

passages.text: You may eat any animal that has a split hoof divided in two and that chews the cud.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel food laws.
\r\nGod told Israel which animals they may eat.
\r\nYou may eat any animal with these traits.
\r\nThe animal must have a split hoof.
\r\nThe hoof must be divided in two.
\r\nThe animal must chew the cud.
passages.original: וְכָל־ בְּהֵמָ֞ה מַפְרֶ֣סֶת פַּרְסָ֗ה וְשֹׁסַ֤עַת שֶׁ֙סַע֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י פְרָס֔וֹת מַעֲלַ֥ת גֵּרָ֖ה בַּבְּהֵמָ֑ה אֹתָ֖הּ תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: But of those that chew the cud or have a completely divided hoof, you are not to eat the following: the camel, the rabbit, or the rock badger. Although they chew the cud, they do not have a divided hoof. They are unclean for you, as well as the pig; though it has a divided hoof, it does not chew the cud. It is unclean for you. You must not eat its meat or touch its carcass.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel laws about clean and unclean animals.
Some animals chew the cud or have a split hoof.
But you must not eat certain animals from these groups.
Do not eat the camel.
Do not eat the rabbit.
Do not eat the rock badger.
These animals chew the cud.
But they do not have a divided hoof.
They are unclean for you.
Do not eat the pig.
The pig has a divided hoof.
But it does not chew the cud.
It is unclean for you.
Do not eat their meat.
Do not touch their carcasses.
passages.original: אַ֣ךְ אֶת־ זֶ֞ה לֹ֤א תֹֽאכְלוּ֙ מִמַּֽעֲלֵ֣י הַגֵּרָ֔ה וּמִמַּפְרִיסֵ֥י הַפַּרְסָ֖ה הַשְּׁסוּעָ֑ה אֶֽת־ הַ֠גָּמָל וְאֶת־ הָאַרְנֶ֨בֶת וְאֶת־ הַשָּׁפָ֜ן כִּֽי־ מַעֲלֵ֧ה גֵרָ֣ה הֵ֗מָּה וּפַרְסָה֙ לֹ֣א הִפְרִ֔יסוּ טְמֵאִ֥ים הֵ֖ם לָכֶֽם׃ וְאֶת־ הַ֠חֲזִיר כִּֽי־ מַפְרִ֨יס פַּרְסָ֥ה הוּא֙ וְלֹ֣א גֵרָ֔ה טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶ֑ם מִבְּשָׂרָם֙ לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֔לוּ וּבְנִבְלָתָ֖ם לֹ֥א תִגָּֽעוּ׃ס

passages.text: Of all the creatures that live in the water, you may eat anything with fins and scales, but you may not eat anything that does not have fins and scales; it is unclean for you.
passages.sermon:
God gives instructions about animals that live in the water.
You may eat any animal that lives in the water if it has fins and scales.
If an animal in the water does not have fins and scales, you must not eat it.
That animal is unclean for you.
passages.original: אֶת־ זֶה֙ תֹּֽאכְל֔וּ מִכֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמָּ֑יִם כֹּ֧ל אֲשֶׁר־ ל֛וֹ סְנַפִּ֥יר וְקַשְׂקֶ֖שֶׂת תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃ וְכֹ֨ל אֲשֶׁ֧ר אֵֽין־ ל֛וֹ סְנַפִּ֥יר וְקַשְׂקֶ֖שֶׂת לֹ֣א תֹאכֵ֑לוּ טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: You may eat any clean bird, but these you may not eat: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture, the red kite, the falcon, any kind of kite, any kind of raven, the ostrich, the screech owl, the gull, any kind of hawk, the little owl, the great owl, the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey, the cormorant, the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, or the bat.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel food laws.
God called Israel a holy people.
God said, “You may eat any clean bird.”
God also said, “You must not eat certain birds.”
You must not eat the eagle.
You must not eat the bearded vulture.
You must not eat the black vulture.
You must not eat the red kite.
You must not eat the falcon.
You must not eat any kind of kite.
You must not eat any kind of raven.
You must not eat the ostrich.
You must not eat the screech owl.
You must not eat the gull.
You must not eat any kind of hawk.
You must not eat the little owl.
You must not eat the great owl.
You must not eat the white owl.
You must not eat the desert owl.
You must not eat the osprey.
You must not eat the cormorant.
You must not eat the stork.
You must not eat any kind of heron.
You must not eat the hoopoe.
You must not eat the bat.
passages.original: כָּל־ צִפּ֥וֹר טְהֹרָ֖ה תֹּאכֵֽלוּ׃ וְזֶ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ תֹאכְל֖וּ מֵהֶ֑ם הַנֶּ֥שֶׁר וְהַפֶּ֖רֶס וְהָֽעָזְנִיָּֽה׃ וְהָרָאָה֙ וְאֶת־ הָ֣אַיָּ֔ה וְהַדַּיָּ֖ה לְמִינָֽהּ׃ וְאֵ֥ת כָּל־ עֹרֵ֖ב לְמִינֽוֹ׃ וְאֵת֙ בַּ֣ת הַֽיַּעֲנָ֔ה וְאֶת־ הַתַּחְמָ֖ס וְאֶת־ הַשָּׁ֑חַף וְאֶת־ הַנֵּ֖ץ לְמִינֵֽהוּ׃ אֶת־ הַכּ֥וֹס וְאֶת־ הַיַּנְשׁ֖וּף וְהַתִּנְשָֽׁמֶת׃ וְהַקָּאָ֥ת וְאֶֽת־ הָרָחָ֖מָה וְאֶת־ הַשָּׁלָֽךְ׃ וְהַ֣חֲסִידָ֔ה וְהָאֲנָפָ֖ה לְמִינָ֑הּ וְהַדּוּכִיפַ֖ת וְהָעֲטַלֵּֽף׃

passages.text: All flying insects are unclean for you; they may not be eaten.
passages.sermon: Flying insects are unclean for you.\r\nYou must not eat them.
passages.original: וְכֹל֙ שֶׁ֣רֶץ הָע֔וֹף טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶ֑ם לֹ֖א יֵאָכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: But you may eat any clean bird.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel food laws.
God called Israel a holy people.
God said, “You may eat any clean bird.”
Clean birds are allowed for you to eat.

passages.text: You are not to eat any carcass; you may give it to the foreigner residing within your gates, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to a foreigner. For you are a holy people belonging to the LORD your God. You must not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
passages.sermon:
You are a holy people.
You belong to the LORD your God.
Do not eat any animal that has died by itself.
You may give such an animal to a foreigner living among you.
The foreigner may eat it.
Or you may sell it to a foreigner.
Do not cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
passages.original: לֹ֣א תֹאכְל֣וּ כָל־ נְ֠בֵלָה לַגֵּ֨ר אֲשֶׁר־ בִּשְׁעָרֶ֜יךָ תִּתְּנֶ֣נָּה וַאֲכָלָ֗הּ א֤וֹ מָכֹר֙ לְנָכְרִ֔י כִּ֣י עַ֤ם קָדוֹשׁ֙ אַתָּ֔ה לַיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹֽא־ תְבַשֵּׁ֥ל גְּדִ֖י בַּחֲלֵ֥ב אִמּֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: You must be sure to set aside a tenth of all the produce brought forth each year from your fields.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God gave them laws to follow.
God told them to set aside a tenth of their produce.
This produce comes from their fields.
They must do this every year.
They must give a tenth from all that grows each year.
passages.original: עַשֵּׂ֣ר תְּעַשֵּׂ֔ר אֵ֖ת כָּל־ תְּבוּאַ֣ת זַרְעֶ֑ךָ הַיֹּצֵ֥א הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה שָׁנָ֥ה שָׁנָֽה׃

passages.text: And you are to eat a tenth of your grain, new wine, and oil, and the firstborn of your herds and flocks, in the presence of the LORD your God at the place He will choose as a dwelling for His Name, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always.
passages.sermon:
God chose Israel to be His holy people.
God commanded Israel to worship Him in a special place.
God told Israel to bring a tenth of their grain, new wine, and oil.
God told Israel to bring the firstborn of their herds and flocks.
God told Israel to eat these offerings in His presence.
God said to do this at the place He will choose for His Name.
God wanted Israel to learn to fear Him always.
passages.original: וְאָכַלְתָּ֞ לִפְנֵ֣י׀ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֗יךָ בַּמָּק֣וֹם אֲשֶׁר־ יִבְחַר֮ לְשַׁכֵּ֣ן שְׁמ֣וֹ שָׁם֒ מַעְשַׂ֤ר דְּגָֽנְךָ֙ תִּֽירֹשְׁךָ֣ וְיִצְהָרֶ֔ךָ וּבְכֹרֹ֥ת בְּקָרְךָ֖ וְצֹאנֶ֑ךָ לְמַ֣עַן תִּלְמַ֗ד לְיִרְאָ֛ה אֶת־ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: But if the distance is too great for you to carry that with which the LORD your God has blessed you, because the place where the LORD your God will choose to put His Name is too far away, then exchange it for money, take the money in your hand, and go to the place the LORD your God will choose.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD your God.
God will bless you.
God will choose a special place for His Name.
Sometimes, this place will be far from you.
You may not be able to carry your tithe all the way there.
If the distance is too great, you must do something different.
You must exchange your tithe for money.
You must take the money in your hand.
You must go to the place that the LORD your God will choose.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִרְבֶּ֨ה מִמְּךָ֜ הַדֶּ֗רֶךְ כִּ֣י לֹ֣א תוּכַ֘ל שְׂאֵתוֹ֒ כִּֽי־ יִרְחַ֤ק מִמְּךָ֙ הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֤ר יִבְחַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ לָשׂ֥וּם שְׁמ֖וֹ שָׁ֑ם כִּ֥י יְבָרֶכְךָ֖ יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶֽיךָ׃ וְנָתַתָּ֖ה בַּכָּ֑סֶף וְצַרְתָּ֤ הַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ בְּיָ֣דְךָ֔ וְהָֽלַכְתָּ֙ אֶל־ הַמָּק֔וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִבְחַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then you may spend the money on anything you desire: cattle, sheep, wine, strong drink, or anything you wish. You are to feast there in the presence of the LORD your God and rejoice with your household.
passages.sermon:
God commanded the Israelites to worship Him at the place He would choose for His Name.
If the Israelites could not bring their offerings because the place was too far, they could exchange their offerings for money.
They could take the money to the chosen place.
They could spend the money on anything they desired.
They could buy cattle.
They could buy sheep.
They could buy wine.
They could buy strong drink.
They could buy anything they wished.
They would eat there in the presence of the LORD their God.
They would rejoice there.
They would rejoice with their household.
passages.original: וְנָתַתָּ֣ה הַכֶּ֡סֶף בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁר־ תְּאַוֶּ֨ה נַפְשְׁךָ֜ בַּבָּקָ֣ר וּבַצֹּ֗אן וּבַיַּ֙יִן֙ וּבַשֵּׁכָ֔ר וּבְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּֽשְׁאָלְךָ֖ נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְאָכַ֣לְתָּ שָּׁ֗ם לִפְנֵי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְשָׂמַחְתָּ֖ אַתָּ֥ה וּבֵיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: And do not neglect the Levite within your gates, since he has no portion or inheritance among you.
passages.sermon:
The Levite lives within your gates.
The Levite has no portion among you.
The Levite has no inheritance with you.
Do not neglect the Levite.
passages.original: וְהַלֵּוִ֥י אֲשֶׁר־ בִּשְׁעָרֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א תַֽעַזְבֶ֑נּוּ כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין ל֛וֹ חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ׃ס

passages.text: At the end of every three years, bring a tenth of all your produce for that year and lay it up within your gates.
passages.sermon:
God gave Israel a command.
Every three years, you must do something special.
Take a tenth of all your produce from that year.
Gather this tenth from your harvest.
Bring it to your town.
Store it within your gates.
passages.original: מִקְצֵ֣ה׀ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ שָׁנִ֗ים תּוֹצִיא֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ מַעְשַׂר֙ תְּבוּאָ֣תְךָ֔ בַּשָּׁנָ֖ה הַהִ֑וא וְהִנַּחְתָּ֖ בִּשְׁעָרֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: Then the Levite (because he has no portion or inheritance among you), the foreigner, the fatherless, and the widow within your gates may come and eat and be satisfied. And the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands.
passages.sermon:
The Levite lives among you.
The Levite has no portion or inheritance with you.
The foreigner lives within your gates.
The fatherless lives within your gates.
The widow lives within your gates.
They may come to you.
They may eat.
They may be satisfied.
The LORD your God will bless you.
He will bless you in all the work of your hands.
passages.original: וּבָ֣א הַלֵּוִ֡י כִּ֣י אֵֽין־ לוֹ֩ חֵ֨לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֜ה עִמָּ֗ךְ וְ֠הַגֵּר וְהַיָּת֤וֹם וְהָֽאַלְמָנָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּשְׁעָרֶ֔יךָ וְאָכְל֖וּ וְשָׂבֵ֑עוּ לְמַ֤עַן יְבָרֶכְךָ֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ בְּכָל־ מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָדְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶֽׂה׃ס
